title: Kanklės (Baltic Zither)
summary: Kanklės is a Baltic box zither carved from wood, with a row of strings stretched from a peg bar to the far edge. Played on the lap, it rings softly and is used to accompany and double old village songs.
howToPlay: The strings lie in order of pitch, lowest on the left, each marked with its note name.
A bead glides down a string toward the point where the fingertip plucks. Pluck the string just as the bead arrives.
Start with the slow village song, then try the close-seconds line, where neighbouring strings answer each other in the style of the old canon songs.
Strings keep ringing after a pluck, so quick notes blend into a shimmer, as on the real zither.
rules: Ten strings are tuned to a major scale, from G up to the B above the next G.
A pluck on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra plucks cost points.
Each song is played twice through.
Each string is plucked once per note; the ringing is only for the ear.
heritageNote: Kanklės has been made and played in Lithuania and neighbouring Baltic lands for many centuries, in regional forms with roughly five to a dozen strings. Singers of the old multi-voice songs long used it to double and support their lines.
